body.statement: Under \(\text{ass:rational-box-inputs}\), \(\text{ass:semialgebraic-code}\), \(\text{ass:rational-expression-grammar}\), \(\text{ass:rational-alpha}\), and \(\text{ass:certified-integral-enclosures}\), for every fixed rational \(h>0\) and \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}>0\), longest-edge spatial branch-and-bound applied to the finite encoding in \(\text{def:certifiable-response-program}\) terminates after finitely many subdivisions and emits \(\mathsf{cert}\). A standalone rational-arithmetic checker verifies the finite-disjunct encoding of \(C_n\), every coded-law equality or directed outer enclosure, every coding-cell and query-integral enclosure, all pruning steps, and the total endpoint gaps. On \(p_0\in C_n\), \(\Theta_{\mathrm{cert}}(p_0)\subseteq I_{\mathrm{out}}\); whenever \(\mathcal F_{n,\mathrm{cert}}\ne\varnothing\), \(0\le\operatorname{len}(I_{\mathrm{out}})-(u_{n,\mathrm{cert}}-\ell_{n,\mathrm{cert}})\le4C_{\mathrm{sieve}}h+2\epsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\), where \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\) includes the verified integral-enclosure contribution. For every Autobounds discrete polynomial program expressible in this grammar, the same endpoint guarantee replaces its solver-reported epsilon gap by an independently checkable rational certificate.
body.justification: The explicit grammar is the boundary that turns the abstract lifting into a finite program and a portable certificate.
body.gap: Duarte et al. provide anytime numerical outer bounds and solver-reported epsilon sharpness, whereas exact MILP certificates cover linear deductions; no cited result gives rational certificates for this rational mixed causal semialgebraic grammar.
body.consumer: Autobounds-style analyses can archive a checker and certificate for an explicitly stated structural subclass instead of treating the generating solver as trusted.
